title: Templates
description: How templates work, what they share, and how to pick the right one for your client.

blocks.text: A template in tempjs is a complete Next.js application — not a snippet or theme zip. Each template shares core infrastructure (admin auth, leads, health check, Docker database, FTP uploads) while the overlay layer adds vertical-specific pages and models: rooms for hotels, properties for real estate.

When you run tempjs hotel inside an empty folder, files land directly in that folder. The CLI does not create hotel-website-template as a subdirectory. That design keeps deployment and git repos simple: your client folder is the app root. .tempjs.json records template id and version so tempjs update can diff against upstream later.

All templates support theme presets, font pairings, database flags, and core brand fields. Template-specific flags (e.g. hotel landmark line vs real-estate RERA) are declared in templates.json and mirrored in each template's docs page and command builder. You are not forced to pass every flag — only what you configure appears in non-interactive commands.
